Q: timer using chrono in C++ A:

It has been rightly pointed out by Alan Birtles and Comet, the duration value needs to be an integer type to enable straightforward addition of 'start' and 'duration' and subsequent printing. However, I wanted to allow the user to input timer duration as a fraction of a second. So I save the double input into nanoseconds and save that as an integer duration. Changes made:

std::chrono::nanoseconds timer_duration((long long)(timer*1000000000));

Thank you.

Q: Improving structure of a Java base conversion program A:

The simplest way you can reason about this is to have some sort of intermediate representation. For example, you can convert all numbers to a base of your chosing (e.g. binary), and then have methods to convert from binary to your base. In such a system, you would have an interface that exposes toBinary() and fromBinary(), which convert from and to the respective base (you would have this separately implemented for all the bases you wish to support / it could be generalised for any arbitrary base). Instead of allowing direct trans-base operations, do them in binary, and convert the result at the end.

E.g.:

  1. User enters 112₍₁₀₎

  2. Program converts it to 1111011₍₂₎ (new Base10().toBinary(123))

  3. You convert to the wanted base (new Base16().fromBinary(1111011))

  4. Voila :D

Other notes:

  1. showMenu - you don't need to use \n within the String, you can just call System.out.println two times and System.out.print for the last line.

  2. for (;;) looks unclean, you can simply use while (true) which is much more readable

Q: iOS Build Succeeds, but Displaying Blank Screen Flutter A:

I had the same issue. What worked for me is i completely deleted the iOS folder (Don't forget to backup first). Then I recreated the iOS folder (It made the folder with new configurations like the UI Scene Configurations and the new changes iOS made in the info.plist file). Then i added my permissions and other files that i had and ran it worked successfully.

Obviuosly I have also operations that can be sued to load and store data from memory. Q: How can I activate a virtualenv in Linux? A:

The eval command is used because the regular source or . methods might not work reliably in some container environments. This approach executes the activation script's contents directly

  
eval "$(cat /app/venv/bin/activate)"
